items.title: packaged-reload cleanup reports a leftover senpi-rpc-host-internal dir under Linux disk fsync load
items.body:
## Summary

Under heavy disk fsync load on Linux, the packaged-reload test's cleanup (`cleanUpReloadRun` in `packages/omo-senpi/src/components/ultrawork/packaged-reload-cleanup.test-support.ts`) fails with:

```
error: task host left senpi-rpc-host-internal-<id> behind
```

The test body itself passes in these runs (4 `expect()` calls pass, no body timeout); only the leftover check at line 89-90 fails. The task host exits (the `exited` wait settles before the deadline), but its `senpi-rpc-host-internal-*` directory is still inside the test root.

Refs #10846 (the packaged-reload stall on Linux; this is a separate failure mode seen while investigating it).

## Reproduction (Linux arm64 container, evidence held locally)

- Image: the local receipt image (Ubuntu-based, bun 1.4.3), 4 CPUs, 6 GiB memory.
- Code: a dev-based commit that already contains #10868 (async store admission) and #10871 (longer kill-exit wait).
- Load: three `dd if=/dev/zero bs=1M count=1024 conv=fsync` writers looping on the container disk. A 4 KiB `conv=fsync` probe took 1470 ms, then 5 ms, under that load.
- Command: `bun test --timeout 20000 packages/omo-senpi/src/components/ultrawork/ultrawork-packaged-reload.test.ts`, run 4 times while the writers ran.

| run (in order) | result | test time |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | fail: `task host left senpi-rpc-host-internal-841f6e50 behind` | 18903 ms |
| 2 | fail: `task host left senpi-rpc-host-internal-65e302dd behind` | 10658 ms |
| 3 | pass | 3154 ms |
| 4 | pass | 8627 ms |

All four runs used the same test root under `/tmp` on the container disk (the test hardcodes `/tmp/omo-ulw-reload-` on POSIX; see below). Without the writers the same test passes.

## Expected

After a SIGTERM-driven shutdown the task host removes its own internal directory before it exits, even when the disk is slow; or, if the host had to be SIGKILLed, the cleanup reports that instead of a leftover directory.

## Hypothesis (not proven)

`cleanUpReloadRun` gives SIGTERM 3 s (`DEFAULT_TERM_GRACE_MS`) and then sends SIGKILL. A host whose shutdown is waiting on an fsync on a saturated disk can miss that grace, get SIGKILLed, and so never removes its internal directory. The leftover check then reports the directory, which hides the real event (a SIGKILL). The next step is to record whether each host exited by signal (`signalCode`) and how long SIGTERM took.

## Related hermeticity defect

`ultrawork-packaged-reload.test.ts` line 17 creates its root with `mkdtempSync("/tmp/omo-ulw-reload-")` on POSIX instead of `tmpdir()`, so a runner's `TMPDIR` does not control where the test writes. This will be fixed in its own small PR (Refs #10846). The fix must keep the root short enough for the unix socket path limit.

## Acceptance criteria

- A RED test with a fake host that honours SIGTERM only after a delay longer than the grace shows today's misleading leftover error.
- Cleanup either waits long enough for a slow SIGTERM shutdown within its budget, or reports "host needed SIGKILL" explicitly.
- The packaged-reload test passes under the stress above in repeated runs.

items.title: BUG: UCC fails during package cleanup when using os-dependentLibraries
items.body:
### Description

When using `os-dependentLibraries`, UCC fails during cleanup.

Example configuration from `globalConfig.json`:

```
        "os-dependentLibraries": [
            {
                "name": "charset-normalizer",
                "version": "3.4.1",
                "dependencies": true,
                "platform": "none",
                "python_version": "3.9",
                "os": "linux",
                "target": "linux"
            }
        ]
```

Error when running `poetry run ucc-gen build`:

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/Users/eliykat/Library/Caches/pypoetry/virtualenvs/bitwarden-event-logs-tLbDvKTI-py3.9/lib/python3.9/site-packages/splunk_add_on_ucc_framework/commands/build.py", line 460, in inner_function
    func(*args, **kwargs)
  File "/Users/eliykat/Library/Caches/pypoetry/virtualenvs/bitwarden-event-logs-tLbDvKTI-py3.9/lib/python3.9/site-packages/splunk_add_on_ucc_framework/commands/build.py", line 583, in generate
    install_python_libraries(
  File "/Users/eliykat/Library/Caches/pypoetry/virtualenvs/bitwarden-event-logs-tLbDvKTI-py3.9/lib/python3.9/site-packages/splunk_add_on_ucc_framework/install_python_libraries.py", line 274, in install_python_libraries
    remove_packages(
  File "/Users/eliykat/Library/Caches/pypoetry/virtualenvs/bitwarden-event-logs-tLbDvKTI-py3.9/lib/python3.9/site-packages/splunk_add_on_ucc_framework/install_python_libraries.py", line 436, in remove_packages
    if _remove_package(installation_path, package_name):
  File "/Users/eliykat/Library/Caches/pypoetry/virtualenvs/bitwarden-event-logs-tLbDvKTI-py3.9/lib/python3.9/site-packages/splunk_add_on_ucc_framework/install_python_libraries.py", line 392, in _remove_package
    os.remove(os.path.join(installation_path, path))
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/Users/eliykat/Projects/splunk/output/bitwarden_event_logs/lib/../../bin/normalizer'
```

This appears to have been introduced by #1915, which uses the dependency's `RECORD` file to clean up its files. In this case, the `RECORD` file looks like this:

```
$ cat output/bitwarden_event_logs/lib/linux/charset_normalizer-3.4.1.dist-info/RECORD
../../bin/normalizer,sha256=WnpJW2eHL0nLt7OAW3FEzQa-z76mVV9n13FIVwUop3E,287
[further lines omitted]
```

As the stack trace shows, UCC concatenates this to `/Users/eliykat/Projects/splunk/output/bitwarden_event_logs/lib/../../bin/normalizer`, however the actual file is located in `/Users/eliykat/Projects/splunk/output/bitwarden_event_logs/lib/bin/normalizer`.

This appears to be an upstream pip bug where the `RECORD` file is not updated properly when using `pip install --target`: https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/7658. That bug has been open since 2020, but perhaps there is some workaround that can be implemented in this repository in the meantime.

As this all occurs inside the UCC build code, I wasn't able to implement any workaround from the outside in my own build scripts. I have changed to using an arm-64 runner instead so that I could remove the `os-dependentLibraries` option.

### What UCC version are you using?

6.1.0 but should be present in >= 6.0.0

### Additional System Info

macOS Tahoe 26.2

items.body:
## Why

The owner decided on 2026-10-31 that Syrinx is one app for Windows, Linux and macOS, with only the platform layer written per operating system. That decision in `docs/decisions.md` supersedes D2's Windows-only gate. The Linux branch now needs reviewable acceptance evidence and explicit follow-up slices; the earlier media-engine epic #211 remains separate and is not a prerequisite for ordinary WebKitGTK browsing.

## Architecture and scope

`linux-port` uses WebKitGTK directly through `webkit2gtk`, never wry's GTK backend. A page is a GTK window embedded as an X11 child window of the GPUI window. Under Hyprland, XWayland supplies X11 compatibility; GPUI uses its X11 backend only. WebKit's bubblewrap sandbox remains enabled. Packaging is a portable tarball with per-user scripts.

The core, store, search and UI remain shared with Windows. Native Wayland, macOS, the optional Widevine/Chromium media engine, Linux release signing and browser registration are outside this task. Linux updates need their own owner-approved network decision.

## Current acceptance evidence

Landing PR #226 remains open, with `linux-port` at head **`0aae46c`**. That head includes the earlier B1/B2/B3 PRs, `main` merged in at `bc69c27`, and the 2026-11-03 review fixes. On that head:

- **Windows CI passed:** `cargo xtask check (Windows)` in [run 41771772681](https://github.com/Fledge-Software/Syrinx-app/actions/runs/41771772681) (1h26m), and Formatting.

Before the review, the untouched branch passed 1,696 tests, and the owner-authorized review fixes passed 1,704 on Omarchy/Arch.

The full smoke checklist and 12 screenshots are in `docs/dev/linux-port-acceptance.md` and `docs/dev/linux-port-evidence/`: tabs and restore, page-focused shortcuts, palette placement on the one available monitor, fcitx form/find input, download/cancel, move/resize and clean shutdown. Proprietary NVIDIA was absent; its workaround is not claimed GPU-tested. The packaged executable rendered the loopback page and exited with all seven tracked descendants gone. The portable tarball passed checksums and install/uninstall/reinstall tests exclusively in a scratch HOME. No real registration or owner data was used.

All successful gates used scratch runtime/data/cache/config directories: `/run/user/1000` is read-only in the agent sandbox. DISPLAY, the session bus, fcitx and inherited scale were retained. No test or product change was made for the original runtime-directory failures. The sandbox lacks `/dev/dri`; software-rendered numbers validate the B1 script only, and real machine figures remain for the coordinator.

The owner's “test first, then decide” permission decision and all four review fixes are recorded on linux-port. Geolocation and notification delegation enforcement are verified. Camera and microphone delegation remain unverified because no usable device was present for their positive controls; absence of handler calls does not prove a policy block. The owner retains the prompt for all four kinds, with device-backed checks tracked in #234. Prompts hold the top-level site accountable for sites it embeds. No permission was granted.

## Current PRs and blockers

| Work | Reviewable result | Verification / outstanding work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Landing | #226 → main | Head `0aae46c`: Windows CI green ([run 41771772681](https://github.com/Fledge-Software/Syrinx-app/actions/runs/41771772681)); Linux gate 1,760 + smoke, local only under Xvfb; package/window evidence as above. The owner's desktop checks are #241. No merge authorized. |

| B5 | #222 | Proposed Ubuntu/Xvfb workflow only; no workflow changed. Owner approval required. |

## Slices this epic owns

Each implementation slice uses its own `codex/linux-<topic>` branch from `linux-port`, its own PR, a Linux gate and independent review. Shared-code changes also need Windows CI.

- Landing: reconcile `main` if it moves; record the complete smoke checklist and screenshots; build the package and test install/uninstall in a scratch HOME; open the reviewed `linux-port` → `main` PR. No merge is authorized.
- B1: deliver a repeatable script and measurement document for focused, unfocused and minimized idle CPU, ten synthetic tabs against an installed reference browser, and start-up. items.title: Linux support: native build works, config path and packaging need cleanup
items.body: Hi, I tested IMM locally on Linux and it is already very close to working well. I also noticed there is already a `linux` branch with several useful Linux-related changes, such as: - native 7z/extraction support - Linux hotreload/dependency checks - cross-platform path normalization - some Linux UI fixes On my side, a native release binary works on Linux: ```bash npm run build cargo build --release --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml ``` The app can start, load EF/XXMI paths, scan EFMI mods, and display the mod list. The main remaining issue I found is config file location. There are still many places using relative config paths, for example: ```ts readTextFile("config.json") writeTextFile("config.json", ...) readTextFile(`config${game}.json`) writeTextFile(`config${game}.json`, ...) ``` Files involved include: - `src/utils/init.ts` - `src/utils/filesys.ts` - `src/utils/errorCatcher.tsx` On Linux, this can make configs appear next to the executable, depending on how the app is launched. For example, if installed under `~/.local/bin`, it may create: ```text ~/.local/bin/config.json ~/.local/bin/configEF.json ``` For official Linux support, I think configs should use a stable Tauri app data directory instead, such as `appDataDir()` or `localDataDir()`. I also hit two AppImage packaging issues on Arch/CachyOS: 1. `linuxdeploy` strip failed with `.relr.dyn`, fixed locally with `NO_STRIP=1`. 2. The generated AppImage crashed because the WebKitGTK helper process was missing: ```text WebKitNetworkProcess: No such file or directory ``` So for the first Linux target, a native binary or `.deb` package may be easier than AppImage. I also attached two screenshots from my local Linux build. They show that the app was successfully compiled, launched, and is working well with my EFMI setup.

items.title: Docs wrongly claim the SQLite cache is Linux/macOS-only

milestone.title: Milestone 8: 0.2.1 Post-Release Polish
milestone.description: Fixes for issues surfaced by the 0.2.0 release: the orphaned-tag gap left by #28, config page formatting, and documentation that describes behaviour the plugin does not have.

items.body:
## Description

The README, the 0.2.0.0 release notes and the migration spec all state that the SQLite cache does not work on Windows and silently falls back to an in-memory cache that is lost on restart. **This is not true** — the cache persists on Windows.

The claim was reasoned from the csproj's `RemoveNativeWindowsLibrariesFromPublish` target, which deletes `runtimes/*/native/*.dll` at publish so Jellyfin's `PluginManager` does not throw `BadImageFormatException` trying to load a native DLL as managed. The inference was that with no bundled `e_sqlite3.dll` the cache could not open on Windows. In practice it does: `DtddClientProvider.CreateCache` (`Services/DtddClientProvider.cs:283-298`) only falls back to `InMemoryDtddCache` when opening actually throws, and the Jellyfin host process has already loaded a SQLite provider.

**Complexity:** S

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `README.md:36` — drop "(in-memory on Windows; see Requirements)" from the caching feature bullet
- [ ] `README.md:104` — drop "SQLite on Linux/macOS, in-memory on Windows" from the comment-injection cost note
- [ ] `README.md:156-158` — rewrite the "A platform caveat: the SQLite cache is Linux/macOS-only" section. Keep the real reason the native DLLs are stripped (`BadImageFormatException` disables the whole plugin); remove the claim that this costs Windows its persistent cache
- [ ] `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-18-dtdd-client-migration-design.md:514-518` — keep the `Microsoft.Data.Sqlite.Core` idea as packaging cleanup, drop the "would restore a persistent cache on Windows" rationale
- [ ] 0.2.0.0 release notes — edit the Windows sub-bullet under the caching item
- [ ] Describe the in-memory path as what it is: a generic fallback for any host where the cache file cannot be opened (permissions, read-only volume, missing provider), not a Windows rule

## Notes

The `RemoveNativeWindowsLibrariesFromPublish` target stays. Its reason is unrelated to caching.

## Контекст

При ручной проверке staged Linux candidate `v0.3.20` на реальной ALT Workstation 10.1 пользователь заметил большое количество `.dll` внутри `app/`.

Важно: само расширение `.dll` не означает Windows-only artifact. Self-contained .NET publish под Linux штатно содержит множество managed .NET assemblies с расширением `.dll`.

Однако exact Linux producer artifact из candidate run `34448100127` был дополнительно проинспектирован. В нём отсутствуют `.exe`, `runtimes/win-*` и Windows native binaries, но присутствуют Windows-oriented managed assemblies, в частности:

```text
app/NAPS2.Wia.dll
app/NAPS2.Sdk.Worker.Win32.dll
app/Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting.WindowsServices.dll
app/WindowsBase.dll
app/System.Windows.dll
app/System.Private.Windows.Core.dll
app/System.Security.Principal.Windows.dll
app/Microsoft.Win32.SystemEvents.dll
app/Microsoft.Win32.Registry.dll
app/Microsoft.Win32.Primitives.dll
```

Также присутствует `app/NTwain.dll` — его необходимость для Linux path надо доказать отдельно, а не классифицировать по имени вслепую.

## Текущая причина

`webassist/src/WebAssistant/WebAssistant.csproj` содержит безусловные package references:

```xml
<PackageReference Include="Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting.WindowsServices" Version="10.0.11" />
<PackageReference Include="NAPS2.Sdk.Worker.Win32" Version="1.3.0" />
```

Наряду с cross-platform/Linux dependencies:

```xml
<PackageReference Include="Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting.Systemd" Version="10.0.11" />
<PackageReference Include="WebAssistant.NAPS2.Sdk" ... />
<PackageReference Include="NAPS2.Images.Gdi" Version="1.3.0" />
<PackageReference Include="NAPS2.Images.Gtk" Version="1.3.0" />
```

В `Program.cs` Windows/Linux scanner adapter выбирается по ОС, но WindowsServices currently регистрируется безусловно через `AddWindowsService`, а package graph при `dotnet publish -r linux-x64` всё равно может тащить Windows-oriented managed assemblies.

## Требование

Провести platform-purity audit Linux `linux-x64` publish output и удалить из canonical Linux artifact только те Windows-only dependencies, для которых доказано, что Linux execution/scanning path их не требует.

Не удалять DLL вручную post-publish. Исправление должно выполняться на dependency/build graph level.

## Инварианты

1. Linux artifact остаётся self-contained `linux-x64` и запускается без установленного .NET runtime.
2. Нормальные managed `.dll` не считаются ошибкой только из-за расширения.
3. Windows-only package references должны быть conditionally included только для Windows RID/target, если это возможно без нарушения NAPS2 SDK contracts.
4. Linux-specific dependencies (`Systemd`, GTK/SANE path и реально необходимые NAPS2 assemblies) должны сохраняться.
5. Не удалять `NTwain.dll`, `NAPS2.Wia.dll` или другие assemblies только по имени: сначала доказать dependency/runtime reachability.
6. В Linux ZIP не должно быть Windows native executable/runtime payload (`*.exe`, `runtimes/win-*`, Windows native worker binaries), если отдельный cross-platform contract явно этого не требует.
7. После cleanup Linux scanning enumeration/startup/lifecycle должен оставаться GREEN.
8. Existing same-byte release invariants не ослаблять.

## TDD / acceptance

Добавить regression/audit evidence для реально собранного canonical Linux artifact:

- inventory publish output;
- явно проверять отсутствие доказанно ненужных Windows-only assemblies/native assets;
- доказать успешный startup на Linux;
- доказать Linux scanner path;
- canonical ZIP lifecycle должен использовать exact producer bytes без post-build pruning/repack.

## Target evidence already available

На реальной ALT Workstation 10.1 (Autolycus) staged `v0.3.20` payload успешно запускается напрямую из `app/`, слушает `127.0.0.1:17654`, diagnostic page работает, `/v1/scanners` отвечает HTTP 200. Следовательно issue является package/dependency hygiene task, а не текущей причиной runtime failure.

## Release impact

Текущий `v0.3.20` всё равно не публикуется из-за #186 и #187. Поэтому platform-purity cleanup целесообразно завершить до следующего frozen candidate, если он не требует изменения scanner API semantics.

## Scope boundary

Не менять здесь:

- новый scanner API contract/идентификацию/настройки;
- Windows functional behavior;
- accepted semantic authority v0.2;
- release same-byte invariants.

Если выяснится, что удаление Windows packages требует semantic scanner redesign, остановиться и вынести это в scanner transaction, а здесь сохранить только доказанный packaging cleanup.

items.body:
#1465 puts shared host-side job settlement in `scripts/managed_job_settlement.py`, which is a generically named scheduler helper. That helper then imports `scripts.linux_release.installed_process`, walks `/proc/<pid>/fd` directly, and its dependency validation lists the Linux installed-qualification package layout ([observer imports](https://github.com/paintedwolf-ai/paintedwolf-code/blob/96513d5334/scripts/managed_job_settlement.py#L155), [descriptor inspection](https://github.com/paintedwolf-ai/paintedwolf-code/blob/96513d5334/scripts/managed_job_settlement.py#L181)). That leaves shared verification infrastructure depending on a Linux installed-test subsystem.

## Fix

Settlement is shared: both normal runner tests and installed qualification use it. So:
- The scheduler side owns settlement: ticket binding, the completion lock, result publication and cancellation.
- Process-identity observation is a narrow observer interface that settlement calls.
- The Linux `/proc` observer lives with the existing process-observation owner and is selected by platform. The macOS observer uses the same interface.
- `validate_checkout()` validates only settlement's own dependency graph. A caller that loads more packages, such as installed-qualification wrappers or campaign cleanup, validates its own graph through the same function, passing its module list as an argument. The list isn't hard-coded in the helper.
- Tests: the existing settlement invariants run against a fixture observer and against the real observer for the platform.

Fix this in #1465 before it lands.

items.title: Add real GitHub Actions post-lifecycle tests for `run-post` and package cleanup
items.body:
- **Priority:** P1
- **Category:** Functional correctness / Test architecture (QA §2, §3, §5)
- **Type:** testing
- **Effort:** M
- **Related open issues:** complements 09, 10, 11
- **Labels (suggested):** `tests`, `reliability`

## Problem
The post action is part of the public contract: `action.yml` declares
`dist/delete/index.js` as the post step and gates it with
`post-if: success() && env.INPUT_RUN_POST == 'true'`. Unit tests cover the
cleanup code and example 9 passes `run-post: false`, but the assessment found no
clear end-to-end assertion that GitHub's actual post-action lifecycle runs, is
skipped when requested, and cleans the intended package directories.

This is a production risk because post-action behavior depends on GitHub runner
lifecycle semantics, not only TypeScript functions.

## Evidence
- `action.yml` declares `post` and `post-if`.
- `src/delete.ts` stashes extracted package directories while preserving
  archives/cache.
- `src/input.ts` exports `INPUT_RUN_POST` for `post-if`.
- Assessment: "`post-if` / `run-post` behavior as an actual GitHub post-action
  lifecycle event ... still depends on GitHub runner behavior."

## Proposed solution
1. Add a workflow that runs `uses: ./` with a dedicated `pkgs-dirs` location and
   creates fake extracted package directories plus archive files.
2. Assert after the job/post phase that extracted dirs were stashed and archive
   files/cache were preserved.
3. Add a second job with `run-post: false` and assert no stash directory is
   created.
4. Run on Linux and Windows at minimum; macOS if timing stays reasonable.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Real workflow verifies post cleanup runs when `run-post: true`.
- [ ] Real workflow verifies post cleanup is skipped when `run-post: false`.
- [ ] Assertions cover `pkgs-dirs`, extracted directories, archive files, and
      the `cache` subdirectory.
- [ ] Tests are stable across reruns and clean up after themselves.

## Out of scope
- Unit-level cleanup behavior already covered in `delete.test.ts`.

items.title: Ordinary managed-engine Linux suite exceeds its existing 20-minute budget
items.body:
The unchanged `checks.yml` Linux job passes remotely but repeatedly exceeds its existing 20-minute Go test budget through a managed private Docker engine. Preserve every fixture/assertion and the timeout while diagnosing the local execution cost.

Verified source/run evidence:

- Source `9068eccaab00b42188fa0068f928a47155fc28bc`, ordinary default Bosn 0.1.10 run `52c3aba0-1e43-452e-9a03-efa0429441f0`: 1,157 tests, one skip, 72 timeout rollups; runner package 1200.055s; cleanup failed. The later engine state was exited; no restart was used as proof.
- Source `e667d9bac2e5b73af020fb48bf534d13a690fcee`, published Bosn 0.1.12 state run `75cac99f-5015-4d63-8d27-2b95ed6a64af`: 1,123 tests, one skip, 32 timeout rollups; runner package 1200.051s; cleanup removed the owned engine.
- Reader-fixed source `12b11d6d22805e17852a5cf5c6b6dd66fda15f9a`, published Bosn 0.1.12 run `b2520814-a5d0-4c8a-a384-35080ada0038`: 1,120 tests, one skip, 29 timeout rollups in 1201.472s; total 1342.048s; exit 1; cleanup removed owned engine `f19e293ac036d3a9fd47e33042d46f7de671969e91ef9974baeb1ddd00608a4f`. This stack had zero archive-producer/cancellation-waiter frames after #15's reader fix. The active subtest was `TestRunEvent/basic` for seven seconds, inside `containerReference.tryReadID` reading an attached exec response. This does not prove that seven-second operation caused the suite-wide timeout.
- Same reader-fixed source passes all required remote checks: [Linux job, 12m13s](https://github.com/zackees/act2/actions/runs/37165530263/job/111327534148). Prior e667 remote Linux completed 1,294 tests/one skip in 706.802s.

These rollups are unfinished package/subtest reports after one timeout, not independent assertion failures or proof of flakiness. The published custom-state runs are version-qualified validation, not proof that the normal default installation is integrated. Their outer runner reports act2 0.2.89-act2.3; the Go suite builds the stated candidate source.

Measured observations, not a causal conclusion:

- Private Docker start/die events measured one `local-action-dockerfile` job at 148.45s, while its three action containers lasted 0.21s/1.59s/1.18s. A later execution showed variable action times of 20.39s/15.49s. Recent individual Docker exec lifetimes mostly stayed below 0.1s, maximum 1.964s.
- A separate unchanged ownership operation diagnostic measured tool-store recursive chown at 0.37–0.51s and action-store chown at 0.004–0.007s. This does not support chown as the dominant cause.
- During the final run the host exposed 16 CPUs, load average around 42, ample available memory, and low observed CPU in the private engine/test containers at the prolonged wait. All relevant node/Ubuntu base images were already present. Resource contention, build preparation, stream handling and network waits remain hypotheses.

Next diagnosis: retain complete gotestsum JSON events via its documented `GOTESTSUM_JSONFILE` option and measure provisioning/build/archive/execution phases. Do not add blind `t.Parallel`: existing fixtures share workspace/action caches and global logging. Any bounded concurrency change first needs isolated per-fixture state and tests proving isolation.

Acceptance: the unchanged whole Linux job passes through the managed private engine at the existing timeout, with every current fixture/assertion, coverage and subsequent CLI step preserved; cleanup succeeds; then demonstrate the ordinary normal-state run against the deployed runtime. Focused probes or remote green alone do not satisfy local parity.

Related: #12 (nested Docker workspace), #15 (independently verified archive-reader leak). #11 is a distinct pre-test cleanup-context failure. Raw diagnostics contain private environment values and are intentionally not attached.

items.body:
# Proposal: bounded Linux userspace function tracing with eBPF

## Problem and proposed first slice

A static call graph cannot show whether one named userspace function actually ran. I propose a small optional eBPF provider for one explicitly selected, owned Linux process and one named function or offset. The first slice would observe `uprobe` entry and `uretprobe` return only, for a finite duration, with a PID filter and bounded raw/output records. It would report PID/TID, function identity, entry/return, clock domain, raw evidence, truncation, cancellation, cleanup, and event loss where measurable. Unknown loss would remain unknown. It would not claim whole-program flow or cross-provider total order.

## Authority and limits

Probe attachment changes host tracing state and may require elevated Linux capabilities. The provider would use a bring-your-own tracer; no automatic install, privilege escalation, kernel configuration, default all-process tracing, arbitrary kernel probes, memory writes, or protection-bypass workflow. Target selection and process identity require explicit checks before attaching.

## Evidence available now

A local pure parser prototype accepts only opt-in bpftrace NDJSON `printf` records with a version marker and maps them to a provider-neutral v1 trace batch. It verifies the claimed PID, preserves exact `nsecs(monotonic)` decimal values, and caps projected events at 10000. Protocol-level tests pass, including malformed frames and capacity. This Windows host has no Linux distro, bpftrace, or container runtime; **no real eBPF probe has been run**, so the prototype is not integration evidence. The parser is not in public CLI/MCP.

## Verification required before integration

On an isolated Linux fixture: source-built executable and known call sequence; entry/return and concurrent threads; missing symbol and dynamic library cases; PID identity/reuse; privilege denial; finite-duration stop, early exit and cancellation; output pressure and observable loss; cleanup; public CLI/MCP and installed package. The target and any raw evidence should remain local to that fixture.

## Maintainer decision requested

Is this restricted userspace `uprobe/uretprobe` lane in REA's scope? Which target-ownership, privilege, loss-reporting, and real-platform verification conditions are required? Should the result project to a separate provider-neutral trace batch while reusing existing native-call semantics where applicable?

Related context: [Frida scope discussion #968](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/968). This proposal is separate because its kernel attachment and privilege effects differ.

items.title: clean: remove package artifacts from dev and release profiles
items.body:
Found while revalidating #7412 against `main@aaa0f6b6`.

## Task

Make package `typelisp clean` remove the current package's ordinary artifacts from both supported build profiles, `dev` and `release`, while preserving its target/kind coverage, confinement checks, dry-run output, and refusal to traverse unsafe filesystem nodes.

## Findings

- Package build and run support `--profile dev|release`; the default is `release`.
- `clean` has no profile selector and is documented as removing package build artifacts.
- `clean-package-from-path` in `src/clean_cli_core.tl` enumerates both Linux and Windows object/runtime names, which demonstrates all-variant intent, but every path is produced by the default-profile helpers in `src/build_cli_core.tl`. Those helpers select only `release`.
- A `typelisp build --profile dev` artifact under `target/dev` therefore survives `typelisp clean`. There is no package-clean integration coverage; the selfhost CLI gate builds a dev package but does not clean it.
- The future authoritative-generation migration is #7412. This current-layout repair should land independently and its both-profile coverage must be retained when #7412 replaces conventional-file cleanup.
- No open issue found by package-clean/profile/artifact searches owns this bug.

## Likely files/modules

- `src/clean_cli_core.tl`
- profile-explicit path helpers in `src/build_cli_core.tl`
- `scripts/verify-selfhost-cli-build-run.sh`
- CLI/package cleanup documentation if it currently implies a narrower scope

## Acceptance criteria

- Package clean plans the exact ordinary artifact names for both `BuildProfile.Dev` and `BuildProfile.Release`: assembly, Linux/Windows object, Linux/Windows bin/staticlib runtime artifacts and their runtime-input sidecars, and host TLCI.
- `--dry-run` reports the same existing files that a real clean would remove, in one stable profile/role/target order, without mutation.
- A fixture builds or creates distinct dev and release artifact/sentinel sets, runs clean, and proves both profile sets are removed while unrelated package-root, `target`, profile-directory, cache, lock, documentation, experiment, and outside sentinels remain.
- Missing artifacts remain idempotent success. A failure for one artifact does not authorize deletion outside the existing confined plan and follows the current deterministic status policy.
- Do not add a `--profile` flag or recursively delete `target`. Do not implement generation records, generation GC, or #7412's future cleanup policy here.
- `typelisp fmt`, focused clean tests, selfhost CLI package build/clean integration, full tests, bootstrap/fixpoint, and Linux/Windows CI pass.

## Assumptions / blockers

Ready on current main. The profile-explicit path helpers already exist; this is a clean planner/integration fix. It has no dependency on #7412 or the transaction substrate. #7412 must preserve the resulting all-profile observable behavior when it later migrates clean to authoritative records.

items.title: Bug: carried MSM resource-cleanup patches write through an uninitialized pointer
items.body:
Found during T41 (#688), accepted Stage-B finding F-01 / L-01 and Stage-C punch item PL-001. **Severity: High. Owner: the base integration (#563/#559).** This is a source defect in the audited fork, not a report of an observed crash. The T41 lane makes no source fix.

## Source trace

At audited source `02aab33bd9842610b0d466c9c186454dc14373ee` (unchanged from dispatch `d7dd766659`), both files contain the pre-fix version:

- `projects/ROCKNIX/packages/linux/patches/7.0/0010-msm-resource-cleanup.patch`
- `projects/ROCKNIX/packages/linux/patches/7.2/0010-msm-resource-cleanup.patch`

The first diff adds `cstate->num_mixers = 0;` at patch line 19; `cstate = to_dpu_crtc_state(crtc_state);` remains later, at patch line 37. In the **complete final SM8550 patched function**, the local pointer is declared at line 1441, written through at 1453 and first assigned at 1470. The full function has no earlier initialization; the global-state error return does not initialize the successful path. SM8550's configuration enables `CONFIG_DRM_MSM=y` at line 4461. H700 and GENERIC_X64 do not enable that driver in the configurations read. Both carried patch copies are byte-identical.

Expected: initialize the local pointer before its first dereference. Actual: the first field write precedes initialization. This permits an indeterminate-pointer write on an enabled MSM DPU path. The accepted normal applications all succeed; application success does not establish code correctness.

[Complete final function and numbered trace](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/blob/7e5d1546712df2eb79c585fce663186770d1ceb9/docs/audits/2026_11_02-epic-m6-patches-shipped-kernel/stage-b/corrected/0010-final-function.txt), [accepted refutation](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/blob/7e5d1546712df2eb79c585fce663186770d1ceb9/docs/audits/2026_11_02-epic-m6-patches-shipped-kernel/04-analysis.md#finding-verification-phase-45).

[9416eec2c200ad969d9e421e686fc7cbfdaca36a](https://github.com/ROCKNIX/distribution/commit/9416eec2c200ad969d9e421e686fc7cbfdaca36a), `kernel: msm dp resource cleanup patch fix uninit pointer`, states:

The immutable local history shows the fix moves initialization before the write in both copies. The retained two-path comparison of the audited source against pinned upstream `651150fc88` reports:

```text
2 files changed, 28 insertions(+), 22 deletions(-)
```

Route uptake through the existing base integration; do not repair these carried patches on the T41 audit branch. No upstream submission is needed for an already-fixed upstream defect.

**Already written:** H700, SM8550 and GENERIC_X64 image builds using the fork's pre-fix source since the base consume these pre-fix patch bytes; this audit did not inspect built images or installed devices. Only SM8550's enabled affected driver is established by the configurations read. The base merge corrects future source/builds; installed images remain unchanged until their normal update. No storage schema, migration or cloud write is introduced by this source correction, and no existing device state was read or changed by this audit.

**Can this be done on the VM?** No — the tree, history and accepted final touched-source artifact establish this source defect; nothing a guest shows is a provenance fact. Build, guest and physical-runtime qualification remain outside this source-only lane. No runtime occurrence or runtime fix is claimed.

- [ ] The base integration records `fixed-at` and the contemporaneous `upstream/next` commit; after the merge, `git diff --stat <fixed-at> upstream/next -- projects/ROCKNIX/packages/linux/patches/7.0/0010-msm-resource-cleanup.patch projects/ROCKNIX/packages/linux/patches/7.2/0010-msm-resource-cleanup.patch` is empty, with the two hashes and command output retained.

items.body:
Established on current `main`, `d5a5d58baf65762871a7aafbf81c80563d438257`, using its selected Linux Verus fork `36d65c3f` and runtime manifest `3b385a69…`. This is a failed re-verification, not a demonstrated false proof.

A successful release verification and its unchanged warm call both return Current. Repeating the identical command with only `SAIL_MANAGED_FORCE=1` fails with CLI exit2, an Unknown empty project result, and `SAIL3100` wrapping `SAIL3107` (“selected Cargo targets did not produce proof receipts after a fresh verification”). The actual forced run has no compiler-start record, and Cargo still reports the requested release artifact as fresh.

Minimal recipe with the repository-selected toolchain/runtime:

```sh
cargo verus new --lib origin_fixture
cd origin_fixture
```

Use this `src/lib.rs`:

```rust
use vstd::prelude::*;
verus! { proof fn origin_lemma() { assert(true); } }
```

Then run:

```sh
sail verify --output json --release
sail verify --output json --release
SAIL_MANAGED_FORCE=1 sail verify --output json --release
```

The first call genuinely verifies; the second reuses its report; the final call must genuinely reverify instead of ending in `SAIL3107`.

Source evidence: [`cargo_clean` on main](https://github.com/Chelis-Lang/sail/blob/d5a5d58baf65762871a7aafbf81c80563d438257/crates/sail-verus/src/managed/runner.rs#L858) forwards the owned target directory, package selection and manifest path, but omits the actual `--release`/`--profile`/`--target` selectors. The [pinned Cargo clean implementation](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/blob/5f94df4789f005f9a352888e8355ffc645b7ed0e/src/ops/cargo_clean.rs#L172) chooses a profile and requested/configured target layouts when cleaning packages. The release cache therefore survives this debug-profile cleanup. The native reproduction covers `--release`; the other omitted selectors are source findings, not separately executed reproductions.

The regression was revealed while qualifying #551. Forward the actual Cargo selectors before the Verus separator, retain full package IDs and owned-target boundaries, and cover real profile/target artifacts. Do not weaken the missing-receipt guard or treat a process success as a proof.

Native evidence: EC2 c7i.4xlarge, us-east-1; source/binary/runtime/toolchain guards passed. The fresh-download independently checked packet is `experiments/2026-10-28/acceptance-env551-main-release-force-d5a5d58b-attempt1-native.tgz`, SHA-256 `de839fcd0214278a3d9e4a197d09cde50fb26b8fb2384d932f8b9dcb39515fea`. It includes literal calls, raw outputs, compiler-start inventories and Cargo artifact records. The coherent main baseline build packet has SHA-256 `4b14e79da2b33e106380d6c602c2b176ce5f69f97dc07db8a3d310e958c3117e`.

items.title: Provide an Agent-Safe Linux Cleanup Tool with Informative GNOME Approval

labels.name: blocked
labels.description: Awaiting an external prerequisite or maintainer decision; investigation alone is not a blocker.

items.body:
## Problem

Agents need a reusable Linux cleanup tool that explains a narrowly scoped privileged operation to the user through an informative desktop prompt, waits for a decision, and reports what actually happened. Repositories should not each carry a Bash recipe or invent their own authorization UI.

This is motivated by a real cleanup failure, not a hypothetical hygiene concern. In [WRAP #708](https://github.com/icefoganalytics/wrap/issues/708), API type checks/tests left root-owned compiler/cache directories in a bind-mounted disposable worktree. Normal `git worktree remove` failed with `Permission denied`; Git had removed its registration while leaving part of the directory behind. The wrapper could already be missing during recovery.

[WRAP PR #709](https://github.com/icefoganalytics/wrap/pull/709) proposed a local Bash recipe displaying `sudo chown` targets and waiting for a typed confirmation. The maintainer requested moving this capability upstream as a **general Linux/GNOME safe-cleanup tool with an informative UI prompt for agent use**, rather than maintaining that recipe in WRAP. The observed need is cleanup; changing application-container users/cache initialization is not a prerequisite.

## Requested Outcome

Provide one small reusable tool/integration in this package for agents to request bounded filesystem cleanup or ownership repair. Use existing Linux/GNOME authorization facilities where appropriate rather than a custom password collector. Keep repository-specific artifact paths and resource identity in the caller; do not hard-code WRAP's compiler/cache layout.

The visible approval should distinguish what the agent wants to do from OS authentication: an unexplained sudo/polkit password dialog alone is not informed consent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Before mutation, show a human-readable preview: requesting agent/tool, reason, exact resolved targets, operation (ownership repair versus deletion), scope, required privilege, and important preserved resources. Make destructive/irreversible effects explicit; do not hide the operation behind a generic authentication label.
- Present an informative Linux/GNOME UI approval and wait for affirmative user input. Cancel, close, denial, missing UI/auth prerequisites, and unattended execution must fail closed without mutation or automatic approval. The prompt must remain understandable at the point privilege is requested.
- Do not request privilege for an operation ordinary user permissions already permit. Use bounded operations on explicitly selected, verified disposable artifacts, not arbitrary agent-supplied root shell programs, blanket checkout ownership changes, or global filesystem/Docker cleanup.
- Reject unsafe or ambiguous paths, symlink escapes, and targets whose identity/scope changes between preview, approval, and execution. Approval must apply only to the operation and targets actually displayed, not silently authorize extra targets or future requests.
- Preserve unrelated source/user files, dependencies, persistent data, other worktrees, and shared resources. Any broader cleanup requires a new visible scope/approval, not inference from a parent directory name.
- Give agents a clear result distinguishing approval, authentication failure/cancellation, executed actions, partial failure, and post-action verification. Never collect/log passwords or treat an approved request as proof that cleanup succeeded.
- Support recovery of known leftover artifact paths even if a failed worktree removal has already deleted its registration/wrapper; do not assume every unregistered directory is disposable. Keep Git/database/container lifecycle decisions with their existing owning workflows.
- Integrate the tool into existing cleanup/worktree guidance so agents discover and use it instead of copying per-project shell snippets. Document installation and desktop/session prerequisites. Publish/install verification must exercise the released artifact if one is shipped.
- Validate on disposable artifacts with a real GNOME approval/authentication surface: affirmative action, denial/cancellation, no UI/unattended case, unsafe/changed target, an actual ownership blocker, ordinary-user cleanup after approved repair, and unrelated-file preservation. Do not claim UI or sudo-authentication coverage from a shell-only substitute.

## Existing Coverage and Non-Goals

Completed #390 documents generated-artifact and partial-worktree recovery. Completed #602 inventories/disposes only owned Docker resources. Completed #675 keeps opaque signing prompts under manual control and explicitly did not request a prompt UI. They are related safeguards, not an existing reusable cleanup tool. Bounded all-state cleanup/sudo/GNOME searches and a source-tree filename check found no equivalent tool request; there are no open PRs at filing.

This request is for the observed cleanup/consent gap. No background cleanup daemon, generic privileged command runner, automatic user-data deletion, application container-user migration, or gateway networking change is requested. Keep the implementation small and reuse maintained OS mechanisms.

Learner coverage: no action — explicit maintainer request based on an observed cleanup failure and rejected local recipe; no automatic Learner detection miss is asserted.

### Description

A stopped JavaScript output read can leave its own Table Filter dialog open. Format restoration in `finally` then replaces the original ambiguous Filter-click receipt with `Node procedure is blocked by a mask or dialog`, and JavaScript has no release verifier for the stopped `read` phase. Ordinary shutdown refuses the unsettled operation and the saved package remains locked.

This issue tracks only the owned Table read cleanup in PR #340 / Multica LAB-156 (`01a16ba2-445a-798d-8937-c67ac466f83f`). ### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a saved package containing JavaScript on Loginom 7.4.2 and execute an existing-node operation with exact output reading.
2. Observe an ambiguous Table Filter opening after the native click deadline; the owned Filter dialog is present in the internal journal.
3. The old `finally` attempts Format restoration through that open dialog and loses the primary failure. Releasing the stopped JavaScript `read` is refused.

Expected: clean up only this operation's owned Table draft, restore original formatting and retain the primary failure; allow the existing bounded release verifier. items.title: Run Linux image provisioning inside a Firecracker builder VM
items.body:
Linux image setup currently runs package provisioning and downloaded agent installers inside a host-side chroot. The files are installed into the future guest rootfs, but installer and package-maintenance code executes using the host kernel before Firecracker starts. This makes the selected provisioning sources trusted host setup dependencies.

Move Linux image provisioning into a temporary Firecracker builder VM, following the existing Lima builder approach. This would put provisioning code behind the same VM isolation boundary used for agent execution and reduce the host exposure from a compromised installer or package script.

This is a defense-in-depth improvement to the existing Linux setup architecture, not a confirmed injection vulnerability introduced by Grok support. The discussion arose while reviewing #473, which adds another downloaded installer to that setup flow. Track this independently of that PR.

Proposed approach:

- Prepare the minimal bootable rootfs and access needed to start a temporary Firecracker builder.
- Run package installation, agent installers, configured provisioning scripts, and image cleanup inside the builder VM. Define the minimal preparation that must remain on the host explicitly.
- Give the builder only the network access needed for provisioning; do not forward user credentials or expose the user's workspace by default.
- Verify provisioning completed and required binaries are runnable before publishing an image.
- Shut down the builder before publishing its disk as the golden image, preserving the existing image and metadata if the build fails.
- Bound build time and clean up the VM process, mounts, networking, temporary files, and disks on success, failure, timeout, and interruption. Account for concurrent builds.

Acceptance criteria:

- Linux package and downloaded-agent installation runs inside Firecracker rather than the host chroot.
- Existing profiles and setup options retain their documented behavior, with any compatibility changes made explicit.
- Integration coverage exercises successful builds, failed provisioning, timeout/interruption cleanup, and creation of a working instance from the resulting image.
- Setup and trust-model documentation clearly distinguish the remaining host preparation from VM-contained provisioning.

Relevant implementation: `src/setup.rs` (`build_template`, `install_guest_packages`) and `src/lima.rs` (`run_builder_vm`).

items.body:
## Release pipeline — October 26, 2026

Linux uses the same release pipeline as macOS: shared exact-commit Qualification, normal release builds, signing, artifact staging and verification, and the existing publication steps. Do not add a separate human attestation, reviewer gate or local qualification-bundle approval/upload step. Native/manual field evidence qualifies Milestone 2; recurring automated Linux checks belong in the existing qualification and release gates. The next regular release after milestone completion includes Linux. Actual production publication remains outside milestone closure.

## Milestone boundary — October 26, 2026

Milestone 2 ends when Linux is qualified and ready to publish. The next regular release after milestone completion must include Linux through the existing release pipeline, alongside the other public platforms. Publication is not a separate optional follow-up feature.

Keep the complete declared architectures, packages, desktop/session matrix, macOS regression coverage and exact-artifact evidence. Signing and payload binding, automated qualification and artifact admission through the shared pipeline, release metadata/catalog promotion, apt/dnf, pacman/AUR and Nix/cache delivery, install/update discovery, withdrawal/recovery and documentation must all be implemented and verified through the required nonpublishing or isolated rehearsals before milestone completion. A readiness handoff must identify the exact qualified source/artifacts, required release configuration and normal release procedure; it must not leave another implementation project before Linux can ship.

Actual production signing/publication actions, public repository/cache activation, release/feed or website updates and post-publication install smoke checks occur with that next release. They are not required to close this milestone and are not authorized by this scope update. Final signing transformations must still preserve the verified payload relationship and record final hashes; missing, stale or failed evidence must continue to block release admission. No evidence requirement or publication authority is waived.

## Outcome and evidence

Verify functional parity using the actual Linux release artifacts and prepare the existing pipeline to publish Linux in the next regular release after Milestone 2 completes.

## Source pointers

`docs/dev-tasks.md`; `.github/workflows/{release.yml,qualification.yml}`; `packaging/release-platforms.json`; parent #52 and the Linux support/parity contract.

## Work

- Maintain a release evidence matrix mapping every parity requirement to implementing issue, automated receipt or manual evidence, exact commit and artifact checksum.
- On clean supported systems install the actual amd64/arm64 `.deb` and `.rpm` packages and complete onboarding/provider setup, stored values, project/chat/workflow, tools/MCP, Git SSH+HTTPS, editor/search/review, terminals/background cancellation, browser/scanning/OCR/documents, file lifecycle, notifications and accessibility.
- Exercise lock/suspend/reconnect, crash/restart, data backup/restore and migration, package-manager upgrade, withdrawal, downgrade refusal and removal, missing dependencies/services and constrained disk/memory.
- Close the remaining capability inventory: create and complete linked defect issues for discoveries; an arbitrary feature exclusion is not parity. Document only justified platform differences with equivalent outcomes wherever possible.
- Complete Linux install/troubleshooting/download-verification docs and release notes. Implement and rehearse the catalog/pipeline transition so the next regular release after this milestone includes Linux when required admission passes; production activation happens with that release.

## Acceptance and verification

- Both architectures pass the declared distribution/desktop/session matrix from fresh installs and supported upgrades. No unresolved release-blocking parity rows or missing native/security evidence.
- Published-format artifacts contain every required pinned dependency and function without developer tooling.
- Existing macOS qualification remains green; Linux changes do not regress shared behavior.
- Record the exact release commit, artifact hashes, test results and manual findings. Verify the installed workflows as well as the build.

## Dependencies and boundaries

Parent #52. Depends on all required Linux workstreams and external producer release paintedwolf-ai/paintedwolf-opengrep#13. #211 lifecycle qualification and shared Trash/transcript outcomes remain explicit dependencies; verify current implementation and evidence rather than treating closed-unmerged #428 as a delivery gate.

Planning baseline: reviewed 2026-10-09. Verify current source and delivery state before implementation. Use repository-managed verification; retain exact artifact/commit evidence. Closing this issue requires the implemented outcome, not only a design or a successful build.

## Broad Linux compatibility scope

Public Linux qualification now includes the expanded distro/desktop/service/installation contract in #444 and #731–#736. Required capability rows must have implementing owners and artifact-bound evidence. Retain distinctions between native Wayland, XWayland, X11, containers and installed desktop execution, including both CPU architectures.

Do not reduce release scope to the available amd64 test host or the candidate builder's Ubuntu image. Missing arm64 desktop or other required native evidence remains unverified and blocks the corresponding release claim.

## Nix and NixOS acceptance

Include #932's Nix/NixOS matrix in the release evidence ledger and publication decision. Require #927–#931 outcomes through their individual issues: package closure, installation layout, system integration/trust, developer workflows and owner-managed updates/recovery.

Retain exact source and lock revisions, derivation/output closure identity, helper versions and installed/native evidence for both architectures. Exercise system and user installation modes, native credential custody and fresh system authentication, Nix-on-conventional-Linux, NixOS switch/rollback/GC and schema-safe data recovery. VM or emulated results do not replace required native desktop/security evidence. A package build alone cannot close these rows.

## Artifact-bound publication readiness and admission

Make the acceptance matrix an enforced input to publication. A green source-level Qualification workflow or closed issue count is not installed-artifact evidence.

- Consume the complete #444/#456 matrix, including native pacman #943 and Nix/NixOS #932, performance #455, macOS regression and #933–#939. Record required rows and acceptable evidence tiers so omissions cannot disappear from an aggregate pass.
- Bind each result to the source revision and the actual final package bytes/architecture or Nix closure. Qualify release-intended payloads after final build transformations. If signing changes a package's bytes, retain and verify the explicit pre-sign payload-to-final-signed-artifact relationship and final digest; do not substitute a later rebuild on the strength of the same commit alone.
- Wire Linux promotion/publication to successful candidate, signing, installed and manual-evidence admission. Current `publish-immutable` does not depend on `linux-candidates`; that is acceptable only while Linux stays candidate-only. Public Linux must fail closed when any required artifact or evidence row is missing, stale, failed or unverified.
- Test admission with missing architecture/format, omitted manual evidence, altered package, wrong signer, mismatched source/closure, skipped required probe and evidence from an older candidate. All must refuse publication before production writes.
- Prepare same-version macOS/Linux publication for the next regular release after milestone completion. Pacman/AUR, apt/dnf and Nix delivery each retain their installation-owner and withdrawal semantics. The release procedure must record final published hashes and verify public install paths after publication; executing those production steps is outside this milestone and does not replace prior qualification.

#211 is remaining lifecycle qualification of the implementation on main. Closed-unmerged #428 is not a pending delivery dependency. OpenGrep producer #13 is closed; #49 retains consumer staging and installed scans. #42 is Windows-only.

## Repository and cache delivery gate

Require #50's R2 publication/retention/cache contract for apt/dnf #759, pacman/AUR #942 and the signed Nix binary cache #945. Qualification must include cold-cache substitution on both architectures, exact closure identity, signatures and complete referenced objects.

Before production activation, verify payload/metadata consistency and the required isolated rehearsals for stale/negative caching, interrupted publication, retained old indexes, withdrawal and key rotation. Test through the public custom-domain delivery behavior. Release admission must reject missing objects, mismatched signatures, stale evidence and rehearsal keys. Do not mistake successful bucket upload for a usable package repository or Nix cache.

## Launch evidence priorities — 2026-10-23

The immediate critical path is reproduced launch/mount reliability (#1313), focused protected turn/persistence/reopen and browser evidence (#1330/#196), essential presence/lock/sleep and active-work Quit interactions (#1174/#1144/#1146/#1149), followed by normal landing and qualification of the exact release-intended artifact set.

Current scoped evidence: the user confirms the trial fixes blob writes, confined browsing and editor/chat scrolling. A retained protected mock turn completed tool acquisition, command execution and final reply; its completed turn and exact committed reply blob were independently found after the app stopped. The automated case timed out because its observer assumed explicit session provider/model overrides, a populated finish_reason and a different serialized blob. Reopening after restart remains unverified. Later positive mount/startup runs do not explain earlier protected-app exits or hidden late volumes.

Maintain separate states for demonstrated product defect, missing installed evidence, source acceptance and test-infrastructure failure. None may be silently converted into another. Open implementing branches and field success do not qualify a rebuilt final package.

Do not make generalized GUI/pointer machinery or additional architectural cleanup an acceptance row for its own sake. Prefer existing supported probes or reproducible artifact-bound manual evidence where the row's required tier permits it. Keep enforced rejection of missing/stale/failed/skipped required evidence and the actual human-review/publication authority boundary.

The complete declared architecture/package/environment matrix and all existing acceptance outcomes above remain required. These priorities change execution order and unnecessary infrastructure work, not the public support promise.

## Focused installed reply and restart evidence

One scoped Ubuntu 24.04 GNOME Wayland amd64 deb run at 100% display scaling completed protected tool acquisition, invoked the fixed command, saved the exact canonical reply, and observed identical reply/turn/attempt/tool receipts after restart under a distinct engine process. The raw guest case passed; the canonical campaign correctly remains unverified because the declared 150% and 200% variants and other required cases are incomplete. Both application stops were controlled test stops, so this is not normal Quit approval/cancellation evidence.

This used the existing local trial artifact (application source `8023fab71c`, package SHA-256 `0761b4b3f66e911d242ff66a8a407d309972ef56bc66467fa8a00ec45b5152ef`) and separately pinned qualification driver `cb7236d514` (tree `4afccc3c103cb9c581100e52bd1fcb0cd3d8256a`). It is focused installed evidence, not qualification of an exact public release candidate. Original QA session configuration was restored and the returned session locked. The full declared matrix, browser/security/lock/Quit evidence, normal landing and final candidate qualification remain required.

## Proposed reduction of repeated conversation qualification

[PR #1370](https://github.com/paintedwolf-ai/paintedwolf-code/pull/1370) removes only conversation from uniform display-scale repetition: qualify its shared provider/turn/persistence/restart semantics once at 100% for every unchanged environment, installation, architecture and release. The current catalog retains all 260 such runtime combinations and every support row, while avoiding 520 repeated semantic runs. All other catalog fields and fractional/mixed-scale UI requirements remain unchanged. Provider and approval dialog visibility, focus, overflow and actions are explicitly covered by the existing scale-sensitive input/accessibility checks.

The change is independently source-reviewed and ready for normal CI; it is unmerged and no CI pass is claimed here. Existing captured campaigns retain their original requirements, including the scoped reply/restart result above; no historical evidence is promoted. Other capability reductions require their own source-backed review.

### Protected browser proof — October 23

The focused installed browser-sandbox-composition case passed on the Ubuntu24.04 GNOME Wayland100% diagnostic target: actual product `8023fab71c34251a9325807d7e9919fbab77a03a`, deb SHA256 `0761b4b3f66e911d242ff66a8a407d309972ef56bc66467fa8a00ec45b5152ef`, local driver tree `47d5a8a9b60f540fb91d56455a00999e82ee4c8d`. The normal GUI turn completed real page_open, independently matched the durable invocation/arguments and original canonical page evidence/blob, and persisted the fixed terminal reply. Six observed browser processes passed exact launch/engine ancestry, UID, zero-capabilities, no-new-privileges, seccomp and distinct namespace checks; no selected browser survivors remained after controlled stop. Raw/imported case evidence is byte-identical SHA256 `950f688b7e794fae4bc6845dbfd5c77128606854aa4e13b930c43be4836149c8`. QA marker/GDM/profile custody restored, original QA session locked.

The whole managed invocation remains exit201/admission unverified: capture/download and allowed/denied local-service cases were unselected, other scales and matrix rows are missing. This uses a local diagnostic driver composition; its source PRs still require ordinary parent landing and final-candidate qualification. Controlled stop is not GUI Quit proof. The first browser attempt's reporting failure remains retained; no old evidence was promoted.


## Native credential custody checkpoint — October 25

The pre-release Linux target uses protected native service custody and fresh system authentication for person-held reveal/unlock. items.title: The NuGet cleanup prefix of Linux test containers guards only the first statement of a multi-statement test command
items.body:
## Problem

On a Linux agent, `DockerBuild.ps1` runs a test container with `sh -c "$testNuGetCacheCleanup$Command"`, where the prefix comes from `CleanUpBuildAgent.ps1 -EmitTestCommandPrefix` (`New-TestCommandPrefix`, `src/PostSharp.Engineering.BuildTools/Resources/CleanUpBuildAgent.ps1:162`):

```powershell
return "rm -rf " + ( $words -join ' ' ) + " && "
```

The `&&` guards only the first statement of the test command. When the command of a test contains several statements, for instance `command1; command2; exit 0`, the shell parses it as `(rm -rf ... && command1); command2; exit 0`. When `rm -rf` fails to delete a stale package:

- `command1` is skipped;
- `command2` still runs, against the stale package that the cleanup was meant to remove;
- the container exits with the status of the last statement, so the test can report a pass.

The comment above `New-TestCommandPrefix` states that the `&&` "keeps the test command from running at all", which holds only for a test command made of one statement. The prefix exists because restoring a stale package reports a pass for code that was never tested, so a failed cleanup must stop the whole command.

## Proposed fix

- Make the prefix leave the shell when the cleanup fails, so that no part of the appended command runs, for instance `rm -rf <patterns> || exit 1; `. `||` and `;` keep the expected semantics in POSIX `sh`, and the exit status is non-zero, which fails the test.
- Update the comment of `New-TestCommandPrefix`, and the comment in `DockerBuild.ps1` that describes the prefix, to state the new behavior.
- Add a test of `-EmitTestCommandPrefix` with a multi-statement command whose cleanup fails.
- Regenerate the scripts of the consuming repositories with `Build.ps1 generate-scripts` once the fix is released.

## Context

Found by the Copilot review of metalama/Metalama.Premium#112, which contains a generated copy of the script (`eng/CleanUpBuildAgent.ps1`). The copy is not edited there because it is generated from this repository.

— Claude for @gfraiteur

items.body:
Parent controller: #8950
Exact-source host controller: #9008
Core host leaves: #10676 / #10679 / #10681 / #10684 / #10691 / #10693
Managed/public replay: #9010 / #9012
Support registry: #7122

## Priority / release cut

**Maintained-host breadth rail.** One deep Linux x86_64 exact-source row is sufficient to earn the first narrow actual-client claim. Other OS/architecture/version rows remain independent and must not inherit Linux semantics.

## Problem

A single Lite XL receipt is subject-bound. Process launch differs materially on native Windows (`windows_skip_cmd`, process-tree cleanup), package paths differ by OS/architecture, watcher implementations may differ, and Lite XL/plugin releases can change client behavior without any `perllsp` change.

Without a maintained matrix the project will drift toward two bad shortcuts:

```text
"Lite XL supported" from one exact Linux run
or
re-running an unbounded full semantic journey on every host/version
```

## Objective

Define and execute a tiered exact-host matrix that reuses #10673 and promotes only directly measured rows.

## Matrix model

For each row retain:

```text
Lite XL version/hash
lite-xl-lsp version/ref/hash
language_perl version/ref/hash
platform / execution environment / arch
perllsp subject
registration/package source
core journey subset
watcher/process/platform-specific cells
result/limitations
receipt freshness/invalidation
```

Initial candidates:

```text
Linux x86_64   → deep semantic reference row
Windows x86_64 → bounded real-host identity/start/config/diagnostic/edit/restart/cleanup + Windows process discriminator
macOS arm64    → bounded real-host identity/start/config/diagnostic/edit/restart/cleanup
additional architectures only when package/release topology and real host exist
```

Do not infer macOS x86_64 from arm64, Windows from WSL, or WSL from Linux native.

## Version policy

Before two host versions have direct evidence, support is exact-version/bounded—not a guessed semver range.

Where public docs eventually name a minimum supported Lite XL/plugin version, directly exercise:

```text
minimum named version
current released version
```

A newer upstream commit invalidates only cells affected by changed client behavior, as determined by #10651/receipt invalidation—not every historical row forever.

## Bounded non-reference rows

Non-Linux rows need not duplicate every provider fixture initially. At minimum prove:

```text
exact host/server identity
safe configuration boundary
one diagnostic
one navigation/provider discriminator
one applied edit
position/wire canary where platform path differs
explicit restart
normal close/no orphan
managed artifact resolution where claimed
watcher cell only when directly instrumented
```

Linux remains the deep semantic reference until a reason moves it.

## Negative controls

Fail when:

- Windows native is satisfied by WSL;
- one Lite XL/plugin version is relabeled as a range without another endpoint;
- platform package availability is inferred from source buildability;
- another architecture's `perllsp` asset satisfies a row;
- missing watcher/process instrumentation becomes pass;
- public package row is inferred from exact-source plugin checkout;
- a stale receipt survives a changed load-bearing host/client implementation silently.

## Agent packet

**Suggested branch:** `agent/lite-xl-host-matrix`

**One-PR claim:** support registry has exact maintained host rows and directly measured bounded host receipts for admitted platform/version subjects.

**Conflict key:** `lite-xl.host-matrix`

Use existing canonical host driver/receipt. Do not fork OS-specific support schemas.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Linux deep reference row and bounded non-Linux rows remain dimensionally separate.
- [ ] Native Windows explicitly proves direct `perllsp` launch/process cleanup and cannot inherit WSL.
- [ ] Version ranges exist only when endpoint evidence earns them.
- [ ] Platform/architecture package identities are exact.
- [ ] Missing/unavailable host instrumentation remains `not_proven`.
- [ ] #7122 can invalidate/promote exact rows without a scalar all-platform Lite XL flag.

## Non-goals

No requirement every platform block the first narrow row, no remote/virtual hosts, no arbitrary performance parity, no public managed-package claim without #9012, no architecture inference, and no DAP.

- [Native user-cache root](https://github.com/jaeyoung0509/neati/blob/70c0c62ac6681b1697c7fb428326cb6d6dd234b7/crates/neati-platform/src/paths.rs#L735-L750) is macOS-only, even though literal `${XDG_CACHE_HOME}` catalog expansion exists. [Freedesktop thumbnail layout](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/thumbnail/latest/directory.html) documents the named cache hierarchy.
- BleachBit also recognizes packaged browser roots ([Firefox](https://github.com/bleachbit/bleachbit/blob/8e6a42edbdbe9b3294729f8ad9cd9615b8828f13/cleaners/firefox.xml#L18-L54), [Chromium](https://github.com/bleachbit/bleachbit/blob/8e6a42edbdbe9b3294729f8ad9cd9615b8828f13/cleaners/chromium.xml#L20-L65)). - [ ] Define Linux inspection readiness explicitly. Keep Linux cleanup mutation, app uninstall, privileged actions and unsupported platform features unavailable. A read-only status may permit inspection only after the adapter and an executing Linux test exist; frontends and browser fixtures must consume the generated capability contract.
- [ ] Resolve the XDG cache root once through PlatformEnvironment with unset/empty/default and invalid-override behavior tested. Register Linux-only exact thumbnail subroots (normal/large/x-large/xx-large/fail as supported), not a recursive home or complete `~/.cache` sweep. Legacy `~/.thumbnails` can be separately labelled when present.
- [ ] Measure bounded metadata only. Never read or export PNG URI metadata, browsing history, credentials, configuration or app content to infer disposal. Report nonzero observed bytes, missing/inaccessible/partial reasons and the exact namespace. Observed results have zero selected/cleanable bytes and cannot produce a deletion plan.
- [ ] Add a Linux Rust/architecture test job consuming the shared frontend artifact where needed, with injected roots and temporary fixtures covering no-link traversal, symlinked ancestors, invalid roots, sparse/hard-link accounting, cancellation, permission failure, bounds and overlap. Verify both direct IPC mutation refusal and UI disabled actions.
